newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to unveil deregulation package next week.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to unveil deregulation package next week.

text.p: Indonesia has again delayed a a package of deregulation measures aimed at boosting economic efficiency and will now announce the measures next week, State Secretary Murdiono said on Friday.
He said President Suharto had agreed to the deregulation measures but suggested some fine-tuning.
"The president has in general agreed on the deregulation package proposed by ministers," Murdiono told reporters after a meeting between Suharto and economic ministers.
"There are policies outlined by the president that we need to elaborate on. It will need time," he said. "We hope to announce the package next week."
He said the package is aimed at boosting economic efficiency and competitiveness and will cut some levies.

"In general, we will increase our economic efficiency, boost competitiveness and cut unnecessary levies," he said. "We also will boost the domestic economy, especially for the medium- and small-scale businesses."
Earlier, finance ministry officials said the package had been finalised and was likely to be announced after the meeting.

The deregulation measures were previously scheduled for last month but Coordinating Minister for Economics and Finance Saleh Afiff was quoted as saying on June 20 there were some differences of opinion among ministers involved in drawing up the proposals.
On June 25, Murdiono said the package was at the final stage, indicating the differences had been resolved.

The Indonesian government routinely unveils measures aimed at bolstering economic growth ahead of the meeting of the Consultative Group on Indonesia (CGI), a grouping of donor nations and financial institutions led by the World Bank.
"We also reported (to the president) on the preparations for the coming CGI meeting," Murdiono said.
The group is to meet later this month in Tokyo.
The World Bank, in its latest report on Indonesia, said that Indonesia's deregulation programme was losing momentum and that this could affect the health of the economy.

Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita has said Indonesia expects to obtain some $5 billion in foreign aid this year. the World Bank has recommended that aid be maintained at last year's level of $5.26 billion.
